title: Assess every route category of an interlocking

facts.note: validator runs in CONFIRM and is confirm-blocking; it assesses every interlocking in the plan, changed or not
source only declares validation subject_kind=interlocking; an observer must enumerate interlockings as subjects from the plan model — file-level identification is not established by the source

fires: At CONFIRM, an interlocking has only nominal routes and leaves alternate, error and exception unaddressed
At CONFIRM, an existing interlocking that was not edited in this change still lacks an assessment for error or exception
An interlocking has a nominal route plus one token alternate route while error and exception have neither routes nor a typed not-applicable basis
An interlocking marks error as not-applicable using free prose instead of a basis from the closed vocabulary
An interlocking marks a category not-applicable while that category already carries routes
An interlocking declares nominal as not-applicable
doesNotFire: At CONFIRM, every interlocking has nominal routes and alternate, error and exception each have routes or a typed not-applicable basis, with no category both routed and marked not-applicable
Phases other than CONFIRM, e.g. drafting unrelated plan documents — but any invalid interlocking, edited or not, still fails once the plan reaches CONFIRM

given: An interlocking in the plan; its route space is the closed category set nominal, alternate, error, exception
when: The plan is assessed at CONFIRM (every interlocking, changed or not)
then: Assess every category explicitly: nominal carries one or more routes, and alternate, error and exception each carry routes or a typed not-applicable basis from the closed vocabulary.
prefer: For alternate, error and exception, state what happens: write the routes or pick the matching closed-vocabulary basis
Ensure that, as assessed at CONFIRM, no category carries both routes and a not-applicable basis
avoid: One token alternate route while error and exception stay unwritten
Declaring nominal not-applicable (it is the executed path)
A not-applicable basis on a category that carries routes (stale contradiction)
why: 'At least one non-nominal route' is gamed by a token alternate; assessing each category forces stating what happens on each, and a typed not-applicable stops the escape eroding into copy-pasted prose.
evidence: For each interlocking, every category of {nominal, alternate, error, exception} has an assessment status; nominal has >=1 route; each other category has routes or a closed-vocabulary not-applicable basis, never both
verifier_detail: Category space is closed: nominal, alternate, error, exception; a missing category is a finding
nominal: requires >=1 route; nominal is the executed path, so any not-applicable basis on nominal is a finding

alternate/error/exception: pass iff routes present XOR not-applicable basis present; basis must be a member of the closed vocabulary (free prose is a finding); routes AND basis together is a contradiction finding (prevents stale assessments)

validation: family=presence, template=conditional_requirement, variant=planner_train_route_category_assessment, phase=CONFIRM, enforcement=confirm-blocking, subject_kind=interlocking; applies to every interlocking regardless of whether it changed
failure_evidence fields: interlocking_id, category, route_ids, not_applicable_basis, assessment_status
The members of the closed not-applicable vocabulary are not enumerated in this convention; the validator's accepted basis list is authoritative
audit: Source term ids: category_space, nominal_requires_routes, typed_not_applicable, no_contradiction

additions.text: The members of the closed not-applicable vocabulary are not enumerated in this convention; the validator's accepted basis list is authoritative
additions.justification: Reviewer flagged that planners cannot pick a valid basis without knowing where the vocabulary is defined; the source names a closed vocabulary but does not list it, so this points to the validator (the source's implementation) without inventing members or obligations.
